rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: The ratio of HCF to LCM of the least composite number and the least prime number is :
rows.solution:
The least composite number is 4 and the least prime number is 2.

HCF\((4, 2) = 2\) and LCM\((4, 2) = 4\), so HCF : LCM \(= 2 : 4 = 1 : 2\), which is option (A) \(1:2\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: The roots of the equation \(x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0\) are :
The next term of the A.P. : \(\sqrt{6}, \sqrt{24}, \sqrt{54}\) is :
rows.solution:
\(\sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\) and \(\sqrt{54} = 3\sqrt{6}\), so the A.P. is \(\sqrt{6}, 2\sqrt{6}, 3\sqrt{6}, \ldots\) with common difference \(\sqrt{6}\).

The next term is \(4\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{16 \times 6} = \sqrt{96}\), which is option (B) \(\sqrt{96}\).

rows.stem: The distance of the point \((-1, 7)\) from x-axis is :
rows.solution:
The distance of a point from the x-axis is the absolute value of its y-coordinate: \(|7| = 7\).

This is option (B) \(7\).

rows.stem: What is the area of a semi-circle of diameter 'd' ?
rows.solution:
The radius is \(\dfrac{d}{2}\), so the area of the semi-circle is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\pi\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{8}\pi d^2\).

This is option (C) \(\dfrac{1}{8}\pi d^2\).

rows.stem: The empirical relation between the mode, median and mean of a distribution is :
rows.solution:
The empirical relation between the three measures of central tendency is Mode \(= 3\,\)Median \(- 2\,\)Mean.

This is option (A) Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: The pair of linear equations \(2x = 5y + 6\) and \(15y = 6x - 18\) represents two lines which are :
rows.solution:
Write the equations as \(2x - 5y - 6 = 0\) and \(6x - 15y - 18 = 0\).

\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{-5}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{-6}{-18} = \dfrac{1}{3}\).

All three ratios are equal, so the lines are coincident, which is option (C) coincident.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If \(\alpha, \beta\) are zeroes of the polynomial \(x^2 - 1\), then value of \((\alpha + \beta)\) is :
rows.solution:
For \(x^2 - 1\), the sum of the zeroes is \(-\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{0}{1} = 0\). (The zeroes are 1 and \(-1\).)

This is option (D) \(0\).

rows.stem: If a pole 6 m high casts a shadow \(2\sqrt{3}\) m long on the ground, then sun's elevation is :
rows.solution:
If \(\theta\) is the sun's elevation, \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{6}{2\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\), so \(\theta = 60^\circ\).

This is option (A) \(60^\circ\).

rows.stem: \(\sec\theta\) when expressed in terms of \(\cot\theta\), is equal to :
rows.solution:
\(\sec\theta = \sqrt{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\cot^2\theta}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\cot^2\theta + 1}{\cot^2\theta}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \cot^2\theta}}{\cot\theta}\).

This is option (C) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \cot^2\theta}}{\cot\theta}\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Two dice are thrown together. The probability of getting the difference of numbers on their upper faces equals to 3 is :
rows.solution:
Of the 36 outcomes, a difference of 3 comes from (1, 4), (4, 1), (2, 5), (5, 2), (3, 6) and (6, 3): 6 outcomes.

\(P = \dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{1}{6}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{1}{6}\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta QPR\). If AC = 6 cm, BC = 5 cm, QR = 3 cm and PR = x; then the value of x is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - triangles ABC and QPR drawn side by side with AC = 6 cm, BC = 5 cm, QR = 3 cm and PR = x marked; the stem states every value and the correspondence. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
\(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta QPR\) matches A with Q, B with P and C with R, so AC corresponds to QR and BC to PR.

\(\dfrac{AC}{QR} = \dfrac{BC}{PR}\) gives \(\dfrac{6}{3} = \dfrac{5}{x}\), so \(x = 2.5\) cm, which is option (B) \(2.5\) cm.

rows.stem: The distance of the point \((-6, 8)\) from origin is :
rows.solution:
Distance from the origin \(= \sqrt{(-6)^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\).

This is option (D) \(10\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, PQ is a tangent to the circle with centre O. If \(\angle OPQ = x\), \(\angle POQ = y\), then \(x + y\) is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that Q is the point of contact (so OQ is a radius) is shown only in the drawing; the stem names the tangent PQ but not where it touches. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
PQ touches the circle at Q, so the radius OQ is perpendicular to the tangent: \(\angle OQP = 90^\circ\).

In triangle OPQ, \(x + y + 90^\circ = 180^\circ\), so \(x + y = 90^\circ\), which is option (B) \(90^\circ\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O such that OT = 4 cm, \(\angle OTA = 30^\circ\), then length of TA is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that A is the point of contact (so OA is a radius) is shown only in the drawing; the stem names the tangent TA but not where it touches. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
TA touches the circle at A, so \(OA \perp TA\) and triangle OAT is right-angled at A.

\(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{TA}{OT}\), so \(TA = 4 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2\sqrt{3}\) cm, which is option (A) \(2\sqrt{3}\) cm.

rows.stem: In \(\Delta ABC\), \(PQ \parallel BC\). If PB = 6 cm, AP = 4 cm, AQ = 8 cm, find the length of AC.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that P lies on AB and Q on AC is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
\(PQ \parallel BC\), so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem \(\dfrac{AP}{PB} = \dfrac{AQ}{QC}\).

\(\dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{8}{QC}\) gives \(QC = 12\) cm, so \(AC = AQ + QC = 8 + 12 = 20\) cm, which is option (B) \(20\) cm.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If \(\alpha, \beta\) are the zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = 4x^2 - 3x - 7\), then \(\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)\) is equal to :
rows.solution:
For \(4x^2 - 3x - 7\): \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{3}{4}\) and \(\alpha\beta = -\dfrac{7}{4}\).

\(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = \dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha\beta} = \dfrac{3/4}{-7/4} = -\dfrac{3}{7}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{-3}{7}\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that the card drawn is not an ace is :
rows.solution:
A pack has 4 aces, so \(52 - 4 = 48\) cards are not aces.

\(P(\text{not an ace}) = \dfrac{48}{52} = \dfrac{12}{13}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{12}{13}\).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The probability that a leap year has 53 Sundays is \(\dfrac{2}{7}\).

**Reason (R) :** The probability that a non-leap year has 53 Sundays is \(\dfrac{5}{7}\).
rows.context: In the question number 19 and 20, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option out of the following :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A leap year has 366 days, that is 52 weeks and 2 extra days. The 2 extra days can be any of 7 pairs (Sunday-Monday, Monday-Tuesday, ..., Saturday-Sunday), and 2 of these contain a Sunday. So \(P(53 \text{ Sundays}) = \dfrac{2}{7}\), and the Assertion is true.

A non-leap year has 365 days, that is 52 weeks and 1 extra day, which is a Sunday in 1 case out of 7. So the probability is \(\dfrac{1}{7}\), not \(\dfrac{5}{7}\), and the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** a, b, c are in A.P. if and only if \(2b = a + c\).

**Reason (R) :** The sum of first n odd natural numbers is \(n^2\).
rows.context: In the question number 19 and 20, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option out of the following :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
If a, b, c are in A.P., then \(b - a = c - b\), that is \(2b = a + c\); and conversely \(2b = a + c\) gives \(b - a = c - b\). So the Assertion is true.

\(1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + (2n - 1) = \dfrac{n}{2}[1 + (2n - 1)] = n^2\), so the Reason is true.

But the sum of odd numbers has nothing to do with the condition for three numbers to be in A.P., so the Reason does not explain the Assertion. This is option (B).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their LCM is 180. What is the HCF of these numbers ?
rows.solution:
Let the numbers be \(2x\) and \(3x\). Since 2 and 3 have no common factor, their LCM is \(6x\).

\(6x = 180\) gives \(x = 30\), so the numbers are 60 and 90.

HCF\((60, 90) = 30\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If one zero of the polynomial \(p(x) = 6x^2 + 37x - (k - 2)\) is reciprocal of the other, then find the value of k.
rows.solution:
Let the zeroes be \(\alpha\) and \(\dfrac{1}{\alpha}\). Their product is 1.

For \(6x^2 + 37x - (k - 2)\), the product of the zeroes is \(\dfrac{c}{a} = -\dfrac{k - 2}{6}\).

So \(-\dfrac{k - 2}{6} = 1\), that is \(-k + 2 = 6\), and \(k = -4\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: Find the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation \(2x^2 - 9x + 4 = 0\).
rows.solution:
For \(2x^2 - 9x + 4 = 0\): \(a = 2\), \(b = -9\), \(c = 4\).

Sum of the roots \(= -\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{9}{2}\).

Product of the roots \(= \dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\).

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation \(4x^2 - 5 = 0\) and hence comment on the nature of roots of the equation.
rows.solution:
For \(4x^2 - 5 = 0\): \(a = 4\), \(b = 0\), \(c = -5\).

Discriminant \(= b^2 - 4ac = 0 - 4(4)(-5) = 80\).

Since \(80 > 0\), the roots are real and distinct.

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: If a fair coin is tossed twice, find the probability of getting 'atmost one head'.
rows.solution:
The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. At most one head means no head or exactly one head: HT, TH, TT, which is 3 outcomes.

\(P(\text{at most one head}) = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

rows.stem: Evaluate \(\dfrac{5\cos^2 60^\circ + 4\sec^2 30^\circ - \tan^2 45^\circ}{\sin^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 30^\circ}\)
rows.solution:
\(\sin^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 30^\circ = 1\), so the denominator is 1.

\(5\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 4\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 - (1)^2 = \dfrac{5}{4} + \dfrac{16}{3} - 1 = \dfrac{15 + 64 - 12}{12} = \dfrac{67}{12}\).

The value is \(\dfrac{67}{12}\).

rows.stem: If A and B are acute angles such that \(\sin(A - B) = 0\) and \(2\cos(A + B) - 1 = 0\), then find angles A and B.
rows.solution:
\(\sin(A - B) = 0\) gives \(A - B = 0^\circ\) ... (1)

\(2\cos(A + B) - 1 = 0\) gives \(\cos(A + B) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(A + B = 60^\circ\) ... (2)

Adding (1) and (2): \(2A = 60^\circ\), so \(A = 30^\circ\) and \(B = 30^\circ\).

rows.stem: How many terms are there in an A.P. whose first and fifth terms are \(-14\) and 2, respectively and the last term is 62.
Which term of the A.P. : 65, 61, 57, 53, ................. is the first negative term ?
rows.solution:
\(a = 65\) and \(d = 61 - 65 = -4\).

Let \(a_n\) be the first negative term: \(a + (n - 1)d < 0\), so \(65 - 4(n - 1) < 0\), that is \(69 - 4n < 0\) and \(n > \dfrac{69}{4} = 17\dfrac{1}{4}\).

The least whole number greater than \(\dfrac{69}{4}\) is 18. Check: \(a_{17} = 65 - 64 = 1\) and \(a_{18} = 65 - 68 = -3\).

The 18th term is the first negative term.

rows.stem: Prove that \(\dfrac{\sin A - 2\sin^3 A}{2\cos^3 A - \cos A} = \tan A\)
rows.solution:
LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin A - 2\sin^3 A}{2\cos^3 A - \cos A} = \dfrac{\sin A(1 - 2\sin^2 A)}{\cos A(2\cos^2 A - 1)}\).

Write \(\sin^2 A = 1 - \cos^2 A\): \(1 - 2\sin^2 A = 1 - 2(1 - \cos^2 A) = 1 - 2 + 2\cos^2 A = 2\cos^2 A - 1\).

So LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin A(2\cos^2 A - 1)}{\cos A(2\cos^2 A - 1)} = \dfrac{\sin A}{\cos A} = \tan A =\) RHS.

rows.stem: Prove that \(\sec A(1 - \sin A)(\sec A + \tan A) = 1\).
rows.solution:
LHS \(= \sec A(1 - \sin A)(\sec A + \tan A) = \dfrac{1}{\cos A}(1 - \sin A)\left(\dfrac{1}{\cos A} + \dfrac{\sin A}{\cos A}\right)\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{\cos A}(1 - \sin A)\dfrac{(1 + \sin A)}{\cos A} = \dfrac{1 - \sin^2 A}{\cos^2 A} = \dfrac{\cos^2 A}{\cos^2 A} = 1 =\) RHS.

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: Find the value of 'p' for which the quadratic equation \(px(x - 2) + 6 = 0\) has two equal real roots.
rows.solution:
\(px(x - 2) + 6 = 0\) is \(px^2 - 2px + 6 = 0\), with \(a = p\), \(b = -2p\), \(c = 6\).

Equal real roots need the discriminant to be zero: \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\), so \(4p^2 - 24p = 0\), that is \(4p(p - 6) = 0\).

So \(p = 0\) or \(p = 6\). For \(p = 0\) the equation becomes \(6 = 0\), which is not a quadratic at all, so \(p = 0\) is rejected.

\(p = 6\).

rows.stem: A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing on the top of the 75 m high tower observes two cars at angles of depression of \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\), which are approaching the foot of the tower. If one car is exactly behind the other on the same side of the tower, find the distance between the two cars. (use \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
rows.solution:
Let AB be the tower, with B its top and A its foot, so \(AB = 75\) m. Let P and Q be the positions of the two cars on the highway, P nearer the tower. BX is the horizontal line through B.

The angles of depression equal the angles of elevation at the cars (alternate angles): \(\angle BPA = \angle XBP = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle BQA = \angle XBQ = 30^\circ\).

In right triangle APB: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{AP} = \dfrac{75}{AP}\), so \(AP = \dfrac{75}{\sqrt{3}} = 25\sqrt{3}\) m.

In right triangle AQB: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{AQ} = \dfrac{75}{AQ}\), so \(AQ = 75\sqrt{3}\) m.

Distance between the cars \(= PQ = AQ - AP = 75\sqrt{3} - 25\sqrt{3} = 50\sqrt{3} = 50 \times 1.73 = 86.5\) m.

rows.stem: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is \(60^\circ\) and the angle of depression of its foot is \(30^\circ\). Determine the height of the tower.
rows.solution:
Let AC be the cable tower of height h m, with A its top and C its foot, and let ED be the building, with E its top and D its foot, so \(ED = 7\) m. Draw EB perpendicular to AC, so \(BC = ED = 7\) m, \(BE = CD\) and \(AB = (h - 7)\) m.

The angle of elevation of A from E is \(\angle AEB = 60^\circ\), and the angle of depression of C from E is \(\angle BEC = 30^\circ\). Since \(BE \parallel CD\), \(\angle ECD = \angle BEC = 30^\circ\).

Let \(CD = x\) m. In right triangle EDC: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{DE}{CD} = \dfrac{7}{x}\), so \(x = 7\sqrt{3}\) and \(BE = 7\sqrt{3}\) m.

In right triangle ABE: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BE}\), so \(\dfrac{h - 7}{7\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\), giving \(h - 7 = 21\) and \(h = 28\).

The height of the tower is 28 m.

rows.stem: D is a point on the side BC of a triangle ABC such that \(\angle ADC = \angle BAC\), prove that \(CA^2 = CB.CD\)
rows.solution:
In triangles CBA and CAD:

\(\angle C = \angle C\) (common), and \(\angle BAC = \angle ADC\) (given).

So \(\Delta CBA \sim \Delta CAD\) (AA similarity).

Their corresponding sides are proportional: \(\dfrac{CB}{CA} = \dfrac{CA}{CD}\).

Cross-multiplying, \(CA^2 = CB \cdot CD\).

rows.stem: If AD and PM are medians of triangles ABC and PQR, respectively where \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\), prove that \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AD}{PM}\).
rows.solution:
AD and PM are medians, so \(BC = 2BD\) and \(QR = 2QM\).

\(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\), so \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{BC}{QR} = \dfrac{2BD}{2QM} = \dfrac{BD}{QM}\).

In triangles ABD and PQM: \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{BD}{QM}\), and \(\angle B = \angle Q\) (corresponding angles of the similar triangles ABC and PQR).

So \(\Delta ABD \sim \Delta PQM\) (SAS similarity), and their corresponding sides are proportional: \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AD}{PM}\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A student was asked to make a model shaped like a cylinder with two cones attached to its ends by using a thin aluminium sheet. The diameter of the model is 3 cm and its total length is 12 cm. If each cone has a height of 2 cm, find the volume of air contained in the model.
rows.solution:
Radius of each cone \(=\) radius of the cylinder \(= \dfrac{3}{2}\) cm.

Height of each cone \(H = 2\) cm, so the height of the cylinder is \(h = 12 - 2 \times 2 = 8\) cm.

Volume of air \(=\) volume of the cylinder \(+\) volume of the two cones

\(= \pi r^2 h + 2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 H = \pi r^2\left(h + \dfrac{2}{3}H\right) = \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{2}\left(8 + \dfrac{2}{3} \times 2\right)\)

\(= \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{9}{4} \times \dfrac{28}{3} = 66\) cm\(^3\).

rows.stem:
The monthly expenditure on milk in 200 families of a Housing Society is given below :

| Monthly Expenditure (in ₹) | 1000-1500 | 1500-2000 | 2000-2500 | 2500-3000 | 3000-3500 | 3500-4000 | 4000-4500 | 4500-5000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of families | 24 | 40 | 33 | \(x\) | 30 | 22 | 16 | 7 |

Find the value of \(x\) and also, find the median and mean expenditure on milk.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: Represent the following information algebraically (in terms of \(x\) and \(y\)).
rows.context:
Two schools 'P' and 'Q' decided to award prizes to their students for two games of Hockey ₹ \(x\) per student and Cricket ₹ \(y\) per student. School 'P' decided to award a total of ₹ 9,500 for the two games to 5 and 4 students respectively; while school 'Q' decided to award ₹ 7,370 for the two games to 4 and 3 students respectively.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a photograph of two trophies; every number is in the passage. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
School P gives ₹ \(x\) to each of 5 hockey students and ₹ \(y\) to each of 4 cricket students, ₹ 9,500 in all: \(5x + 4y = 9500\) ... (1)

School Q gives the same prizes to 4 and 3 students, ₹ 7,370 in all: \(4x + 3y = 7370\) ... (2)

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: What is the prize amount for hockey ?
rows.context:
Two schools 'P' and 'Q' decided to award prizes to their students for two games of Hockey ₹ \(x\) per student and Cricket ₹ \(y\) per student. School 'P' decided to award a total of ₹ 9,500 for the two games to 5 and 4 students respectively; while school 'Q' decided to award ₹ 7,370 for the two games to 4 and 3 students respectively.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
The prizes satisfy \(5x + 4y = 9500\) ... (1) and \(4x + 3y = 7370\) ... (2).

Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 4: \(15x + 12y = 28500\) and \(16x + 12y = 29480\). Subtracting, \(x = 980\).

The prize amount for hockey is ₹ 980.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: Prize amount on which game is more and by how much ?
rows.context:
Two schools 'P' and 'Q' decided to award prizes to their students for two games of Hockey ₹ \(x\) per student and Cricket ₹ \(y\) per student. School 'P' decided to award a total of ₹ 9,500 for the two games to 5 and 4 students respectively; while school 'Q' decided to award ₹ 7,370 for the two games to 4 and 3 students respectively.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: What will be the total prize amount if there are 2 students each from two games ?
rows.context:
Two schools 'P' and 'Q' decided to award prizes to their students for two games of Hockey ₹ \(x\) per student and Cricket ₹ \(y\) per student. School 'P' decided to award a total of ₹ 9,500 for the two games to 5 and 4 students respectively; while school 'Q' decided to award ₹ 7,370 for the two games to 4 and 3 students respectively.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
Solving \(5x + 4y = 9500\) and \(4x + 3y = 7370\) gives \(x = 980\) and \(y = 1150\).

For 2 hockey students and 2 cricket students the total prize is \(2(x + y) = 2(980 + 1150) = 2 \times 2130 =\) ₹ 4,260.

rows.stem: Taking O as origin, coordinates of P are \((-200, 0)\) and of Q are \((200, 0)\). PQRS being a square, what are the coordinates of R and S ?
rows.context:
Jagdish has a field which is in the shape of a right angled triangle AQC. He wants to leave a space in the form of a square PQRS inside the field for growing wheat and the remaining for growing vegetables (as shown in the figure). In the field, there is a pole marked as O.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a squared grid with the x- and y-axes, O at the origin, P and Q marked on the x-axis as (-200, 0) and (200, 0), the square PQRS, B on the y-axis, and the line CA through S and B with C on the x-axis; the passage says the layout is 'as shown in the figure', and which side of PQ the square stands on is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
PQ lies on the x-axis with \(PQ = 200 - (-200) = 400\), and in the figure the square stands above PQ. So R is 400 units directly above Q and S is 400 units directly above P.

\(R(200, 400)\) and \(S(-200, 400)\).

rows.stem: What is the area of square PQRS ?
rows.context:
Jagdish has a field which is in the shape of a right angled triangle AQC. He wants to leave a space in the form of a square PQRS inside the field for growing wheat and the remaining for growing vegetables (as shown in the figure). In the field, there is a pole marked as O.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the coordinates of P and Q, (-200, 0) and (200, 0), are given in part (i) and labelled in the drawing; this part's own text does not state them. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
The side of the square is \(PQ = 200 - (-200) = 400\) units, since \(P(-200, 0)\) and \(Q(200, 0)\) lie on the x-axis.

Area of square PQRS \(= 400 \times 400 = 160000\) square units.

rows.stem: What is the length of diagonal PR in square PQRS ?
rows.context:
Jagdish has a field which is in the shape of a right angled triangle AQC. He wants to leave a space in the form of a square PQRS inside the field for growing wheat and the remaining for growing vegetables (as shown in the figure). In the field, there is a pole marked as O.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the coordinates of P and Q, (-200, 0) and (200, 0), are given in part (i) and labelled in the drawing; this part's own text does not state them. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: the printed value is \(\sqrt{3200}\) or \(400\sqrt{2}\); \(\sqrt{(400)^2 + (400)^2} = \sqrt{320000} = 400\sqrt{2}\), while \(\sqrt{3200} = 40\sqrt{2}\) is ten times too small.]

The side of the square is \(PQ = 200 - (-200) = 400\) units, since \(P(-200, 0)\) and \(Q(200, 0)\) lie on the x-axis. PR is the hypotenuse of the right triangle PQR:

\(PR = \sqrt{PQ^2 + QR^2} = \sqrt{(400)^2 + (400)^2} = \sqrt{320000} = 400\sqrt{2}\) units.

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: If S divides CA in the ratio K:1, what is the value of K, where point A is \((200, 800)\) ?
rows.context:
Jagdish has a field which is in the shape of a right angled triangle AQC. He wants to leave a space in the form of a square PQRS inside the field for growing wheat and the remaining for growing vegetables (as shown in the figure). In the field, there is a pole marked as O.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the position of C is never stated in words; it is read off the squared grid, as is S (whose coordinates come from part (i)). Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
From the figure, \(C(-600, 0)\), and from part (i), \(S(-200, 400)\); A is \((200, 800)\).

If S divides CA in the ratio \(k : 1\), then by the section formula the x-coordinate of S is

\(\dfrac{k(200) + 1(-600)}{k + 1} = -200\), so \(200k - 600 = -200k - 200\), \(400k = 400\) and \(k = 1\).

(The y-coordinates agree: \(\dfrac{k(800) + 0}{k + 1} = 400\) also gives \(k = 1\).) So S is the mid-point of CA, and \(K = 1\).

rows.stem: What is the total perimeter of the parking area ?
rows.context:
Governing council of a local public development authority of Dehradun decided to build an adventurous playground on the top of a hill, which will have adequate space for parking.

After survey, it was decided to build rectangular playground, with a semi-circular area allotted for parking at one end of the playground. The length and breadth of the rectangular playground are 14 units and 7 units, respectively. There are two quadrants of radius 2 units on one side for special seats.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the rectangular PLAYGROUND (14 Units by 7 Units) with the semicircular PARKING AREA on its 7-unit end and quadrants I and II at the two corners of the far end; every value is in the passage. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The parking area is a semi-circle whose diameter is the 7-unit breadth of the playground, so \(r = \dfrac{7}{2}\) units.

Its perimeter is the arc plus the diameter: \(\pi r + 2r = \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{2} + 7 = 11 + 7 = 18\) units.

rows.stem: What is the total area of parking and the two quadrants ?
rows.context:
Governing council of a local public development authority of Dehradun decided to build an adventurous playground on the top of a hill, which will have adequate space for parking.

After survey, it was decided to build rectangular playground, with a semi-circular area allotted for parking at one end of the playground. The length and breadth of the rectangular playground are 14 units and 7 units, respectively. There are two quadrants of radius 2 units on one side for special seats.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the playground drawing; every value is in the passage. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The parking area is a semi-circle of radius \(\dfrac{7}{2}\) units: area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{2} \times \dfrac{7}{2} = \dfrac{77}{4}\) sq units.

The two quadrants have radius 2 units: area \(= 2 \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2 \times 2 = \dfrac{44}{7}\) sq units.

Total area \(= \dfrac{77}{4} + \dfrac{44}{7} = \dfrac{539 + 176}{28} = \dfrac{715}{28} \approx 25.54\) sq units.

rows.stem: What is the ratio of area of playground to the area of parking area ?
rows.context:
Governing council of a local public development authority of Dehradun decided to build an adventurous playground on the top of a hill, which will have adequate space for parking.

After survey, it was decided to build rectangular playground, with a semi-circular area allotted for parking at one end of the playground. The length and breadth of the rectangular playground are 14 units and 7 units, respectively. There are two quadrants of radius 2 units on one side for special seats.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the playground drawing; every value is in the passage. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Area of the playground \(= 14 \times 7 = 98\) sq units.

The parking area is a semi-circle of radius \(\dfrac{7}{2}\) units: area \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{2} \times \dfrac{7}{2} = \dfrac{77}{4}\) sq units.

\(\dfrac{\text{Area of playground}}{\text{Area of parking}} = \dfrac{98}{77/4} = \dfrac{392}{77} = \dfrac{56}{11}\).

The ratio is \(56 : 11\).

rows.stem: Find the cost of fencing the playground and parking area at the rate of ₹ 2 per unit.
rows.context:
Governing council of a local public development authority of Dehradun decided to build an adventurous playground on the top of a hill, which will have adequate space for parking.

After survey, it was decided to build rectangular playground, with a semi-circular area allotted for parking at one end of the playground. The length and breadth of the rectangular playground are 14 units and 7 units, respectively. There are two quadrants of radius 2 units on one side for special seats.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - which boundaries are fenced is drawn only in the figure: a zigzag fence line runs along the edges of the rectangle, and the parking area's arc is drawn plain. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The playground is fenced along all four sides of the rectangle, as the zigzag line in the figure shows (including the 7-unit side it shares with the parking area), and the parking area is fenced along its curved edge.

Length of fencing \(= 2(l + b) + \dfrac{2\pi r}{2} = 2(14 + 7) + \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{2} = 42 + 11 = 53\) units.

Cost of fencing \(= 53 \times 2 =\) ₹ 106.

(If only the zigzag line drawn in the figure is fenced, the length is 42 units and the cost ₹ 84; the marking scheme's answer is ₹ 106.)
